THIS ROUTE: stand on the seesaw's right arm (the walk is let go on 76, x 268.8). A portal at (232, 150) over the left arm, 165 px from the ring's centre, and one at (247, 40) at the rolling
stone's left (the stone-side point may be anywhere from x 240.5 to 254.5 and y 20 to 55): the stone goes through on tick 158 and drops onto the left arm, which tips left-down under it; the stone
rolls down the arm and along the floor past the flame and meets the left wall at x 32.8 by tick 229. THE CREEP IT LEANS ON: the stone then creeps back along the floor at 0.087 to 0.098 u a tick.
Cause (R3b fix 1, by a data edit of the run): the HELD friction's traction. materials.json builds the stone at held_friction 1 (friction_applied is false: the engine's solver cannot carry the decoded
friction), and a stone that arrives at the wall spinning turns its spin into a drift away from it. With the stone's own decoded friction (0.025, combined 0.158 against the held floor) it rests at
x 30.1 for 1,100 ticks and this route fails (the player is burned on tick 1346, the walk reaching the flame with no stone to cross); of the 86 routes only 2-30 and 3-12 then fail, 2-07 wins a tick
earlier and 1-09 two later (R3b fix 2's census). So the route is to be replaced when the engine's friction step turns friction_applied on, or when the owner settles G10-2 (rows R3-2, G10-14).
